meta: Peasants dance, drink and play the bagpipes at a village fair on a saint's day in Pieter Bruegel the Elder's Peasant Dance, painted about 1567.
about: Peasants dance, drink and play the bagpipes at a village fair held on the feast day of the local patron saint. The big red flag on the building at left marks it as Saint George's day. Wikipedia says the dancers turn their backs on the church and ignore the image of the Virgin Mary on the tree, and that the prominent tavern points to worldly rather than spiritual concerns. Pieter Bruegel the Elder painted it about 1567. Napoleon had it taken to Paris in 1808, and it came back in 1815.

meta: The seven sacraments inside one Gothic church: Rogier van der Weyden and his workshop's altarpiece, painted from 1445 to 1450 in Antwerp's Royal Museum.
about: One Gothic church holds all seven sacraments of the Catholic Church. The left panel has baptism, confirmation and confession, and the right panel has the remaining three, from ordination to the last rites. A crucifixion dominates the center. Behind it a priest raises the Host at the altar. Rogier van der Weyden and his workshop painted it between 1445 and 1450, probably for a church in Poligny. Wikipedia says the central panel may be the only part by his own hand. Two coats of arms in the inner frame probably belong to the patrons.

meta: A woman rides a bull past a village in Utagawa Kunisada's 1836 woodcut of Kanbara, from the Fifty-three Stations of the Tōkaidō.
about: A woman rides a bull with a village in the background. The print is titled Kanbara and belongs to the Fifty-three Stations of the Tōkaidō series. Utagawa Kunisada made the color woodcut in 1836, and the Library of Congress holds it.

meta: An American woman plays the accordion beside a dog and a man in Utagawa Sadahide's Japanese woodcut of 1860.
about: An American woman plays an accordion while a dog sits at her right and a man stands to her left. Utagawa Sadahide made this Japanese color woodcut in 1860, printed on hōsho paper. The Library of Congress holds the print.

meta: A Polish soldier with a rifle stands by the Polish flag on Wladyslaw T. Benda's 1917 lithograph poster, Polish Army in France.
about: A Polish soldier brandishes a rifle next to the Polish flag. The color lithograph poster is titled Polish Army in France, and Wladyslaw T. Benda made it in 1917. It is now in the Library of Congress.

meta: A sailor wades through water carrying a soldier on his shoulder in Henry Reuterdahl's 1918 Navy poster.
about: A sailor wades through water with a soldier on his shoulder. Henry Reuterdahl made this color lithograph poster in 1918. Its slogan says the Navy put them across, and it advertises the service for travel and training to men aged 17 to 35. The Library of Congress holds the poster.

meta: The Grand Canyon fills C. Don Powell's 1938 poster for Grand Canyon National Park, a free government service.
about: The Grand Canyon fills this poster. C. Don Powell made it in 1938 as a color screenprint, and its title calls the national park a free government service. The Library of Congress holds it.

meta: Travelers rest under thatched roofs at Hodogaya on the Tōkaidō Road in Utagawa Hiroshige's 1855 woodcut.
about: Travelers rest beneath thatched roofs at the Hodogaya station on the Tōkaidō Road. The view runs down a valley toward mountains in the distance. Utagawa Hiroshige made this color woodcut in 1855, and the Library of Congress holds it.

meta: Steep cliffs frame Lake Hakone with Mount Fuji behind in Utagawa Hiroshige's 1858 woodcut.
about: Steep cliffs and odd rock formations rise at Lake Hakone, with Mount Fuji in the background. Utagawa Hiroshige made this color woodcut in 1858. The Library of Congress holds the print, titled The lake in Hakone.

meta: A woman looks back through clouds at travelers on the Tōkaidō Road in Utagawa Kunisada's View of Hara, made in 1837.
about: A woman looks back through clouds at travelers on the Tōkaidō Road, with fields and mountains behind them. Utagawa Kunisada made this color woodcut, View of Hara, in 1837. The Library of Congress holds it.

meta: A small red-capped bird perches on a bamboo stake beside a lily plant in Baison's 1890 woodcut.
about: A small red-capped bird perches on a bamboo stake that holds up a lily plant. Baison made this color woodcut in 1890, and it is now in the Library of Congress.

meta: Three women stroll beside a river in the cool evening air in Torii Kiyonaga's woodcut of 1785.
about: Three women stroll beside a river, perhaps the Sumida, and enjoy the cool evening air. Torii Kiyonaga made this color woodcut, titled Cooling off near the river bank, in 1785. The Library of Congress holds it.

meta: The actors Iwai Sagenta and Katsuyama Matagorō on a veranda in Torii Kiyonobu's woodcut of 1705.
about: Two actors, Iwai Sagenta and Katsuyama Matagorō, share a veranda. One reclines on it while the other is about to climb the steps. Torii Kiyonobu made the color woodcut in 1705, and the Library of Congress holds it.

meta: Crowds view cherry blossoms from a pavilion and Ueno Park in Nishimura Shigenaga's woodcut of 1725.
about: Many people crowd a pavilion and the grounds of Ueno Park to view cherry blossoms. Nishimura Shigenaga made this color woodcut in 1725, and the Library of Congress holds it.

meta: The actor Segawa Kikunojō V plays the woman Koharu in Utagawa Toyokuni's 1818 woodcut.
about: The actor Segawa Kikunojō V plays Koharu, a woman's role, in this color woodcut by Utagawa Toyokuni from 1818. It shows the actor in the part, and it is now held by the Library of Congress.

meta: A woman with a parasol stands before a book on women's moral education in Utagawa Kuniyoshi's woodcut of 1843.
about: A woman stands full length and faces right, with a parasol on the ground beside her. Behind her is a book on moral education for women. Utagawa Kuniyoshi made this color woodcut, titled One, in 1843. It is in the Library of Congress.

meta: Pedestrians cross Mannen Bridge with Mount Fuji far off in Katsushika Hokusai's woodcut, Under Mannen Bridge at Fukagawa.
about: Pedestrians cross Mannen Bridge over a river while boats pass below and someone fishes from a rock. Mount Fuji rises in the distance. The print is Under Mannen Bridge at Fukagawa by Katsushika Hokusai, a color woodcut dated 1890 in the Library's catalog, and the Library of Congress holds it.

meta: Gods in human form fill a great room at the Izumo shrine in Utagawa Sadahide's 1857 woodcut.
about: Many gods in human form fill a large room at the great shrine at Izumo. Utagawa Sadahide made this color woodcut in 1857, and the Library of Congress holds it.

meta: A head-and-shoulders Greek figure holding a print advertises the WPA Federal Art Project exhibition in Pennsylvania, Katherine Milhous, 1936.
about: A head-and-shoulders portrait of a Greek figure holding a print advertises an exhibition of the WPA Federal Art Project in Pennsylvania. Katherine Milhous made the color woodcut poster in 1936. The Library of Congress holds it.

meta: An antelope hunt from a Navajo drawing advertises the Indian Court at the 1939 Golden Gate International Exposition, a poster by Louis B. Siegriest.
about: An antelope hunt taken from a Navajo drawing fills this poster for the Indian Court exhibit at the Golden Gate International Exposition in San Francisco. Louis B. Siegriest made the color silkscreen in 1939, and the Library of Congress holds it.

meta: Leonardo da Vinci's La Belle Ferronnière in the Louvre has carried several names for its sitter, none certain.
about: Nobody is sure who the woman in this portrait by Leonardo is. By the seventeenth century the title tied her to a ferronnier, an ironmonger, and to a rumored mistress of Francis I. Later she was tentatively named as Lucretia Crivelli, a lady-in-waiting at Milan, and a London exhibition in 2011 listed Beatrice d'Este as a possible sitter. Bernard Berenson gave the Louvre picture to Bernardino de' Conti. Herbert Cook first suggested Boltraffio, but in 1904 he withdrew that and saw Leonardo's own hand.
